title: A section of an invertible sheaf avoids any finite set on an affine scheme
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $E\subseteq |X|$ be a finite set of points, not necessarily closed. There exists $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$ such that, for every $x\in E$, the image of its germ $s_x$ in $L_x/\mathfrak m_xL_x$ is nonzero. Here $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is the local ring, $\mathfrak m_x$ its maximal ideal, and $\kappa(x)=\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 0F20, properties-lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section (lines 5327–5332), specialized to affine X and W=X; also the explicit invocation in Tag 0BUT, divisors-lemma-finite-trivialize-invertible-upstairs.

proof.text: Use strong induction on the cardinality of the finite set $E$, with $X$ and $L$ fixed. If $E=\varnothing$, the zero section satisfies the assertion. Assume the assertion holds for every smaller finite subset of $|X|$.

source.place: Tag 0F20, properties-lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section, empty case and induction on the number of points

proof.text: If distinct $x,y\in E$ satisfy $x\leadsto y$, apply induction to $E\setminus\{x\}$. Its section $s$ is nonzero at $y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes], $X_s=\{w:s(w)\ne0\}$ is open. An open containing $y$ contains its generalization $x$, so this section also works on $E$. Hence it remains to treat nonempty $E$ with no specializations between distinct points.

source.place: Tag 0F20, properties-lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section, induction step, remove a generalization; openness is Modules Tag 01CY, modules-lemma-s-open

proof.text: Choose $z\in E$ and put $F=E\setminus\{z\}$. Induction gives $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$ nonzero at every point of $F$. If $s(z)\ne0$, this already works on $E$. Otherwise $s(z)=0$. Since no $x\in F$ specializes to $z$, apply [lem-sfb-affine-finite-point-scalar-separation] to get $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ with $f(x)=0$ for $x\in F$ and $f(z)\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 0F20, properties-lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section, induction step, separate the new point from the earlier ones

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-invertible-section-fibre-correction] to $X,L,F,z,s,f$. It supplies $t$ such that $v=s+ft$ has $v(z)\ne0$ and $v(x)=s(x)\ne0$ for all $x\in F$. Thus $v$ works on $E=F\cup\{z\}$, completing the induction. This includes $F=\varnothing$ and requires no closedness of the points.
